To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

passage feedback (pf), which featured interactive query refinement, was more effective than document feedback (df), which featured automatic query refinement, for the first use, but was comparable to df for later uses.
Passage feedback (pf) was more difficult to use than document feedback (df), though performance of the two systems was comparable after a single use.

(1) passage feedback was more difficult to use than document feedback; (2) passage feedback was not significantly more effective than document feedback in our experiments; (3) passage feedback may have the potential to be more effective than document feed-back, given a more user-friendly interface; and (4) the performance of passage feedback was affected by learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a passage retrieval system.
the evaluation of passage feedback as an interactive retrieval technique.
the development of a user-centered information retrieval system that incorporates the user's knowledge into the retrieval process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pf and df were comparable in performance, but the learning curve for pf may be steeper.
pf and df performed similarly, but that pf is more difficult to learn.
pf was not as good as df, but it was not as bad as we thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new system for interactive retrieval and we have shown that it is possible to use this system for effective interactive retrieval.
pf, which features interactive query expansion, can be used to improve retrieval performance.
the passage feedback system, though not as effective as the document feedback system, is still a viable option in interactive information retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRIS framework is a useful tool for conducting controlled experiments in information retrieval.

the passage feedback system is more difficult to use, and that the difficulty may be due to the fact that the passage feedback is more interactive and requires the searcher to be more actively involved in the search process.
we can use IRIS to compare the effects of two feedback methods on searchers' performance.
